paper.paper_scope: Establishing the correlation between the composition and microstructure of low-density Fe-Mn-Al-C austenitic steels using machine learning (classification and regression), predicting κ-phase existence, the (γ+κ) dual-phase region at 500-600°C, the single γ region, and κ-phase volume fraction, with experimental validation on Fe-30Mn-8Al-1C steel.
paper.title: Deciphering the composition-microstructure correlation in low-density FeMnAlC steels with machine learning

aliases: annealed at 1000°C for 15 min, water-quenched, and aged at 550°C for 2 h
processes.description: Induction melted under Ar atmosphere; 25 kg as-cast ingot homogenized at 1200°C for 2 h, forged to 60×60 mm billet; homogenized at 1050°C for 100 min; hot-rolled to 12 mm plate and air-cooled; cold-rolled with 75% thickness reduction at room temperature; annealed at 1000°C for 15 min; water-quenched to room temperature; aged at 550°C for 2 h.
processes.process_name: Homogenization, hot/cold rolling, 1000°C annealing + water quenching, 550°C aging

source.reason: Full thermo-mechanical processing route used to prepare the experimental Fe-30Mn-8Al-1C steel, ending in the aged terminal state at 550°C/2h.

The experimental validation sample combines the Fe-30Mn-8Al-1C alloy with the full processing route ending in 550°C/2h aging; characterized as a single-phase austenitic low-density steel with κ-carbide precipitates.

unmapped_findings: The machine-learning classification/regression predicts four features: existence of the κ phase (Y1), the (γ+κ) dual-phase region at 500-600°C (Y2), a single γ region (Y3), and κ-phase volume fraction (Y4).

Al and C (especially Al) govern the phase structure: for 30 wt% Mn, the κ phase requires an Al content of at least about 4 wt%; the (γ+κ) region at 500-600°C corresponds to Al 4.5-9.3 wt% and C 0.4-1.1 wt%.

Dataset: 448 samples with 10 features (Fe, Mn, Al, C plus 6 descriptors) collected from literature and JMatPro v9.0 phase-balance data; 298 samples for the κ volume fraction regression after elimination of missing data.
